Information: IRAPUATO, REIMAGINED is a website about Irapuato and its future. It shows problems in our city and how we can make it better by 2050. It talks about water, parks, pollution, and climate change. It also gives ideas about how people can help. This is a student project, not an official government website.
Source: Project editorial concept; Plan Municipal de Desarrollo Irapuato 2050

Information: What will Irapuato look like in 2050? What can we do today to make it better? For example, saving water, keeping parks clean, and using less plastic can help our community.
Source: Project editorial concept; Plan Municipal de Desarrollo Irapuato 2050

Information: Our goal is to help people understand what is happening in Irapuato. We use simple information, pictures, and activities to explain local problems. We also want people to think about how they can help their city.
Source: Project editorial concept; Plan Municipal de Desarrollo Irapuato 2050

Information: This goal is about having clean water for everyone. We use water every day to shower, brush our teeth, wash clothes, and cook. But water is limited, so we need to take care of it and avoid wasting it.
Source: The Global Goals — SDG 6

Information: This goal is about making cities better places to live. Think about clean streets, safe parks, good buses, and places where people can walk or ride bikes. Everyone should be able to enjoy their city.
Source: The Global Goals — SDG 11

Information: This goal is about taking care of our planet and preparing for climate change. For example, very hot days, heavy rain, and changes in weather can affect our daily lives. We need to protect nature and make better decisions for the future.
Source: The Global Goals — SDG 13

Information: Water, cities, and climate are connected. A bigger city needs more water, houses, roads, and services. Trees and parks help the environment, too. For example, protecting green spaces is one way to make our city better.
Source: The Global Goals — SDGs 6, 11, and 13

Information: Irapuato has a plan to improve the city by 2050. It includes better public spaces, transportation, the environment, and people's quality of life. The main idea is to make Irapuato a better place to live. Our website uses this plan as a reference.
Source: IMPLAN Irapuato — Plan Municipal de Desarrollo 2050

Topic: Environmental priorities identified by the municipality
Information: Irapuato has different environmental problems that need attention. Some examples are air pollution, trash, climate change, and the loss of plants and animals. The city also wants people to learn how to protect nature and save water.
Source: Government of Irapuato — Programa de Protección y Preservación del Ambiente

Information: Most of Irapuato's water comes from underground water sources called aquifers. Think of them as natural water reserves under the ground. The main source is the Irapuato Valle aquifer, and another source is Silao-Romita. The municipal document also says that water use in the main aquifer has restrictions.
Source: Government of Irapuato — Programa de Gobierno Municipal 2024–2027, environmental diagnosis

Information: According to the 2020 Census, 98.61% of Irapuato had water service. In rural areas, the number was 94.94%. This means that almost 99 out of every 100 people in the municipality had water service. These numbers are from 2020, not today.D13
Source: Government of Irapuato — Programa de Gobierno Municipal 2024–2027, citing INEGI 2020

Topic: Water extraction data cited in municipal planning
Information: A municipal document reports that in 2020, 37 million cubic meters of water were taken from underground sources in one year. It also reports 81 working wells, 10 wells in reserve, and 11 that were not working. Think of wells as places that help bring underground water to the surface. These are historical figures, not current 2026 numbers.
Source: Government of Irapuato — Programa de Gobierno Municipal 2024–2027, citing CONAGUA/JAPAMI planning

Information: Have you ever thought about how much water you use every day? You use it when you shower, wash your hands, drink water, or clean your house. Schools, farms, and factories also need water. We should learn where it comes from and how to take better care of it.
Source: Project research prompts; SDG 6; JAPAMI / municipal planning reference

Information: Irapuato has protected natural areas such as Cerro de Arandas and Los Encinos. A municipal document reports that together they cover almost 7,000 hectares. These places are important because they protect plants, animals, and nature. The number comes from that document and should be checked before being presented as current.
Source: Government of Irapuato — Programa de Gobierno Municipal 2024–2027, environmental section

Information: A municipal document reports that Irapuato lost around 15% of its forest vegetation between 2000 and 2018. This means that some areas lost trees and plants during those years. Trees are important because they provide shade and help nature. This is an old statistic, not a measurement of what is happening today.
Source: Government of Irapuato — Programa de Gobierno Municipal 2024–2027, environmental diagnosis

Topic: Environmental issues described in municipal planning
Information: Some environmental problems in Irapuato are air pollution, trash, climate change, and the loss of natural areas. These problems can affect our health and the places where we live. For example, too much trash in the streets can make our neighborhoods dirty.
Source: Government of Irapuato — Programa de Gobierno Municipal 2024–2027

Information: Burning trash, tires, or farm waste creates smoke that can pollute the air. Breathing polluted air can affect our health, and burning materials can also cause fires. For example, burning a pile of trash in an empty space can affect people living nearby. The municipality mentions 072 and 911 as reporting options; check which number is appropriate before using it.
Source: Government of Irapuato — Environmental awareness notice, May 24, 2025

Information: Parks, gardens, and plazas are important parts of a city. They give us places to walk, play sports, meet friends, and relax. Irapuato's Parks Plan 2050 wants to improve these spaces and connect them better. It also identifies problems with their maintenance and distribution.
Source: IMPLAN Irapuato — Plan Maestro del Sistema de Parques 2050

Information: The PMDUOET is a plan that helps organize how Irapuato grows. It helps decide where people can build houses, roads, and businesses, and which natural areas should be protected. For example, a new neighborhood needs roads, water, services, and safe spaces.
Source: IMPLAN Irapuato — PMDUOET

Topic: Municipal vision: resilient and sustainable city
Information: A resilient city is a city that can prepare for problems and changes. For example, it should be ready for heavy rain, very hot days, or other environmental challenges. Irapuato's plan wants to protect people, houses, roads, and public spaces. This is a goal for the future, not something that has already been completely achieved.
Source: Government of Irapuato — Programa de Gobierno Municipal 2024–2027

Information: Irapuato's 2050 plan includes better transportation, public buses, bike routes, parks, and green spaces. For example, imagine being able to ride your bike safely to school or having a park near your house. These are ideas in the plan, not projects that are all finished.
Source: IMPLAN Irapuato — Plan Municipal de Desarrollo 2050

Information: MPLAN has documents about environmental problems and risks in Irapuato. These include information about climate change, pollution, natural areas, and possible risks. These documents help us learn more about our city and its future.
Source: IMPLAN Irapuato — plans, studies, and publications

Information: Plastic bags, straws, and foam containers can create a lot of trash. For example, when people throw plastic bags into the street, they can end up blocking drains when it rains. This can contribute to flooding. Irapuato has a local environmental rule about some disposable plastic products, but its current status needs to be checked.
Source: Irapuato — Sistema Municipal de Mejora Regulatoria, Agenda Regulatoria

Information: A better city needs the ideas of its people. The Irapuato 2050 plan included opinions from residents and different groups. For example, students can share ideas about safer streets, cleaner parks, or better public transportation. Our website is also a way to encourage people to participate.
Source: IMPLAN Irapuato — PMD 2050 and Programa de Gobierno

Information: The simulator shows two possible futures for Irapuato. One shows a city that makes better environmental decisions, while the other shows problems that may continue. You can compare both futures and think about what choices could make a difference. These are examples, not real predictions.
Source: Project editorial note; IMPLAN Irapuato; The Global Goals

Topic: Scenario A — Irapuato with sustainable decisions
Information: Imagine Irapuato in 2050 with cleaner parks, better water use, less trash, and safer streets. People and the government work together to protect the city. For example, families save water, schools recycle, and the city takes better care of public spaces. This is an imaginary future.
Source: Illustrative scenario based on PMD Irapuato 2050, PMDUOET, and SDGs 6, 11, and 13

Information: In this future, people and the city use water more carefully. They avoid wasting it, improve water treatment, and reuse water when possible. For example, treated water could be used to water parks instead of always using clean drinking water. This is a possible goal, not a real future statistic.
Source: Illustrative scenario based on SDG 6 and municipal planning

Topic: Scenario A — Indicator: Green and public spaces
Information: Imagine having more clean and well-maintained parks in your city. You could walk, play soccer, ride your bike, or spend time with friends in these spaces. This future imagines better parks and more protection for natural areas.
Source: Illustrative scenario based on IMPLAN — Sistema de Parques 2050 and SDG 11

Topic: Scenario A — Indicator: Climate and environmental resilience
Information: n this future, Irapuato is better prepared for environmental problems. The city protects trees, plans safer spaces, and teaches people about climate change. For example, better planning can help communities prepare for heavy rain and very hot days. It does not mean that all problems disappear.
Source: Illustrative scenario based on PMD Irapuato 2050, municipal climate planning, and SDG 13

Information: Now imagine Irapuato in 2050, but many problems are still there. There may still be challenges with water, trash, pollution, parks, and natural areas. This could happen if people and the government do not give enough attention to these problems. It is an imaginary example, not a prediction.
Source: Illustrative scenario based on municipal environmental diagnosis and SDGs 6, 11, and 13

Information: n this future, people do not save enough water, and the city does not improve water management enough. The problem continues because water is not being used carefully. For example, wasting water every day can make it harder to manage this important resource. This is a possible situation, not a prediction of a water shortage.
Source: Illustrative scenario based on SDG 6 and municipal planning

Information: magine living in a neighborhood with few parks or green areas. There may not be enough places to walk, play, or relax outside. This future shows what could happen if parks and natural areas are not protected or maintained.
Source: Illustrative scenario based on IMPLAN — Sistema de Parques 2050

Information: n this future, Irapuato does not do enough to prepare for climate change and environmental problems. People may not have enough information or protection. For example, communities need plans to prepare for heavy rain and other environmental risks. This is an imaginary situation.
Source: Illustrative scenario based on municipal environmental priorities and SDG 13

Information: Compare Future A and Future B using three topics: water, parks, and climate change. Future A shows positive changes, while Future B shows problems that continue. Think about which future you would prefer for Irapuato and why. Remember, both are imaginary examples, not real statistics.
Source: Project editorial note; IMPLAN Irapuato; The Global Goals

Information: The website has two buttons: "Future A — Sustainable Decisions" and "Future B — Challenges Continue." When you click one, the pictures, descriptions, and information change. You can switch between both options to see how different decisions could change the future of Irapuato.
Source: Project concept based on original 2050 simulator design

Information:
You can save water with small actions every day. For example:
- Turn off the tap while brushing your teeth.
- Take shorter showers.
- Do not leave water running when washing dishes.
- Avoid wasting drinking water.
Small actions help, but the city and its institutions must also manage water properly.
Source: The Global Goals — SDG 6; municipal water-planning sources

Information:
Parks and natural areas belong to everyone, so we should take care of them. You can:
- Avoid throwing trash on the ground.
- Respect plants and trees.
- Keep parks clean.
- Take part in organized community activities.
Even simple actions can help keep these places nice for everyone.
Source: The Global Goals — SDG 11; IMPLAN Sistema de Parques 2050

Information:
We create trash every day, but we can reduce it with simple choices. For example:
- Use a reusable water bottle.
- Take a reusable bag when shopping.
- Avoid unnecessary plastic packaging.
- Separate your trash according to local rules.
Remember that not all materials can be recycled everywhere.
Source: The Global Goals — SDG 11 and SDG 13; municipal regulatory agenda

Information: Do not burn trash, tires, or other materials because they create harmful smoke. You can also learn about air pollution and share information with others. If you see an environmental problem, report it through the correct official channels. Never approach fires or dangerous places.
Source: Government of Irapuato — environmental awareness notice, May 24, 2025

Information: Cars are not the only way to travel. When it is safe and possible, you can walk, ride a bike, use public transport, or share a car. For example, walking to a nearby store instead of using a car can help reduce traffic. Always choose a safe way to travel.
Source: The Global Goals — SDG 11 and SDG 13

Information: Choose an environmental problem in Irapuato and learn more about it. Then share what you discover with your classmates, friends, or family. For example, you can make a small presentation about why saving water is important. Always use reliable information and share your sources.
Source: World's Largest Lesson; The Global Goals

Information: Think about a park, school, or public space that could be better. What would you change? Maybe it needs more trash cans, better lighting, or more plants. Share your ideas with responsible adults or local organizations. Never enter restricted areas or do work without permission.
Source: The Global Goals — SDG 11; IMPLAN Sistema de Parques 2050

Information: People can work together to improve their city. Some activities include cleaning parks, learning about recycling, saving water, and protecting nature. For example, a school group could organize an environmental awareness activity. Always check that an activity is real, safe, and properly organized before joining.
Source: World's Largest Lesson resources; municipal and IMPLAN planning references

Information: Making Irapuato better is not only one person's job. Students, families, schools, businesses, organizations, and the government all have a role. For example, students can reduce plastic use, schools can teach about recycling, and the government can improve public services. Working together is important.
Source: UN Global Compact — SDGs; Plan Municipal de Desarrollo Irapuato 2050

Information: Choose one simple action that you can do to help Irapuato. It could be saving water, using fewer plastic products, keeping parks clean, or sharing useful information. You do not need to change everything in one day. Start with one small action!
Source: Project activity based on The Global Goals and World’s Largest Lesson

Source: Project editorial statement

Information: This section introduces the students who created IRAPUATO, REIMAGINED. It explains why we chose Irapuato and what inspired us to make this project. It can also include our names, our roles, and a video about our work.
Source: Project editorial statement

Information: The futures shown on this website are examples of what Irapuato could look like in 2050. They are not real predictions or official government plans. The scores and indicators are only used to compare ideas. Real statistics must always include their source and year.
Source: Project editorial disclaimer; IMPLAN Irapuato

Information: The numbers on this website come from official documents and other sources. Some numbers are from previous years, so they may not show the current situation. For example, a statistic from 2020 should always be shown with the year 2020. We should never invent numbers when information is missing.
Source: Project editorial disclaimer; Government of Irapuato; IMPLAN

Information: Every information card should include the source where the information comes from. This allows people to check if the information is correct. Pictures, maps, and graphics also need proper credit or permission. It is important to use real information and give credit to its creators.
Source: Project editorial policy; cited official sources
